answer: Network latency profiling ties each computational node to its unique physical distance from the central server, effectively turning the voyage of a data packet into a verifiable spatial fingerprint. Regulatory costs arise when an attacker attempts to spoof these timing variances to mimic a distant reef, as the discrepancy triggers automatic expulsion and loss of all prior processing credits. This enforcement forces adversary infrastructure to be physically spread out, leaving the lagoon of shared network capacity open to genuine, localized participants.
